subject: general
question: Government grants 51st Tiger reserve status for sanctuaries spanning forests of _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The government of India granted the status of the 51st Tiger Reserve to the sanctuaries spanning the forests of Tamil Nadu.
 
• This newly designated tiger reserve is aimed at bolstering conservation efforts for the endangered tiger species in the region.
 
• The reserve includes areas from the Megamalai Wildlife Sanctuary and Srivilliputhur Grizzled Squirrel Wildlife Sanctuary.
 
• This move is expected to enhance biodiversity, protect wildlife habitats, and promote eco-tourism in the state of Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tiger Reserves in India**

 
 
• India is home to more than 70% of the world's tiger population.
 
• Tiger reserves are protected areas dedicated to the conservation of tigers and their habitats.
 
• The Project Tiger initiative, launched in 1973, aims to safeguard and increase the population of tigers in India.
 
• As of the latest data, there are 51 tiger reserves in India, which are monitored and managed by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).
 
 
 
• **Megamalai Wildlife Sanctuary**
 
 
• Located in the Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu, it is known for its rich biodiversity and scenic landscapes.
 
• The sanctuary is home to several species of flora and fauna, including elephants, leopards, and various bird species.
 
• It plays a critical role in water conservation and maintaining ecological balance in the region.
 
 
 
• **Srivilliputhur Grizzled Squirrel Wildlife Sanctuary**
 
 
• Established in 1989, it is named after the endangered grizzled giant squirrel that inhabits the sanctuary.
 
• The sanctuary spans across the districts of Virudhunagar and Madurai in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It provides a habitat for diverse wildlife, including tigers, leopards, Indian giant squirrels, and several bird species.
 
 
 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**
 
 
• NTCA is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, established in 2005.
 
• It oversees the implementation of Project Tiger and other conservation measures across India.
 
• The authority works towards ensuring a viable population of tigers in their natural habitats and protecting them from extinction.
